([[Chino Hills, California]]) | college = [[USC Trojans men's basketball|USC]] (2019–2020) | highlights = * First-team [[List of All-Pac-12 Conference men's basketball teams|All-Pac-12]] ([[2019–20 Pac-12 Conference men's basketball season|2020]]) * 2× [[California Mr. Basketball]] (2018, 2019) }} '''Onyeka Okongwu''' (born December 11, 2000) is an American [[basketball]] player. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[USC Trojans men's basketball|USC Trojans]]. Listed at {{convert|6|ft|9|in|m|2}} and {{convert|245|lbs|kg|0}}, he plays the [[power forward (basketball)|power forward]] and [[Center (basketball)|center]] position. Okongwu was a four-year starter at [[Chino Hills High School]] in [[California]], playing alongside [[Lonzo Ball|Lonzo]] and [[LaMelo Ball]]. As a freshman, he helped his team win the state championship and achieve national success, while being named [[MaxPreps National Basketball Player of the Year awards#Freshman of the Year|MaxPreps co-National Freshman of the Year]]. In his junior and senior seasons, Okongwu led Chino Hills to two more state titles, earning back-to-back [[California Mr. Basketball]] honors. He was considered a five-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] by [[ESPN]] and [[Rivals.com|Rivals]]. In his only college season, Okongwu played for USC and was named to the first team [[List of All-Pac-12 Conference men's basketball teams|All-Pac-12]]. ==High school career== Okongwu attended [[Chino Hills High School]] in [[Chino Hills, California]] and started on the [[varsity team|varsity]] basketball team since his freshman season.{{cite web|last1=Gardner|first1=Michelle|title=After brother's ===Recruiting=== Okongwu finished his freshman season with offers to play college basketball for [[UCLA Bruins men's basketball|UCLA]] and [[USC Trojans men's basketball|USC]].{{cite web|last1=Sondheimer|first1=Eric|title=Chino Hills freshman Onyeka Okongwu offered by UCLA, USC|url=http://www.latimes.com/sports/highschool/varsity-times/la-sp-vi-boys-basketball-chino-hills-freshman-onyeka-okongwu-offered-by-ucla-20160201-story.html|website=[[Los Angeles Times]]|accessdate=December 3, 2017|date=February 1, 2016}} On May 14, 2018, he committed to USC over UCLA and [[Arizona State Sun Devils men's basketball|Arizona State]]. He was drawn to the program because of its proximity and coaching staff. Okongwu left high school as a five-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] on [[ESPN]] and [[Rivals.com|Rivals]] and as a four-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] on [[247Sports.com|247Sports]].{{cite web |last1=Borzello |first1=Jeff |title=Five-star recruit Onyeka Okongwu chooses USC over UCLA, ASU |url=https://www.espn.com/college-sports/recruiting/basketball/mens/story/_/id/23503916/five-star-recruit-onyeka-okongwu-chooses-usc-trojans-ucla-arizona-state |publisher=[[ESPN]] |accessdate=June 11, 2019 |date=May 14, 2018}} {{College athlete recruit start|40=no|collapse=no|year=2019}} {{College athlete recruit entry | recruit = Onyeka Okongwu | position = [[Power forward (basketball)|PF]] | hometown = [[Chino Hills, California|Chino Hills, CA]] | highschool = [[Chino Hills High School|Chino Hills]] (CA) | feet = 6 | inches = 8 | weight = 225 | 40 = | commitdate = May 14, 2018 | rivals stars = 5 | 247 stars = 4 | espn stars = 5 | espn grade = 93 }} {{College athlete recruit end | 40 = | year = 2019 | rivals ref title = USC 2019 Basketball Commitments | scout ref title = | espn ref title = 2019 USC Trojans Recruiting Class | rivals school = usc | scout s = | espn schoolid = 30 | 247 overall = 27 | rivals overall = 30 | espn overall = 20 | accessdate = December 3, 2017 | bball = yes }} ==College career== Okongwu immediately established himself as [[USC Trojans men's basketball|USC]]'s best player.{{cite web |last1=Givony |first1=Jonathan |last2=Wojnarowski |first2=Adrian |title=USC freshman Onyeka Okongwu opts to enter NBA draft |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/28953136/usc-freshman-onyeka-okongwu-opts-enter-nba-draft |publisher=[[ESPN]] |accessdate=April 28, 2020 |date=March 25, 2020}} In his collegiate debut on November 5, 2019, he recorded 20 points, 13 rebounds and a school-record eight blocks to lead the Trojans to a 77–48 victory over [[Florida A&M Rattlers men's basketball|Florida A&M]]. He became the first USC player to post a [[double (basketball)|double-double]] in his debut since [[Taj Gibson]] in 2006.{{cite news |title=Okongwu's double-double leads USC over Florida A&M 77–48 |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401170557 |accessdate=November 19, 2019 |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=November 6, 2019}} On November 19, he scored a career-high 33 points, including 17 free throws, in a 91–84 win over [[Pepperdine Waves men's basketball|Pepperdine]].{{cite web |last1=Nguyen |first1=Thuc Nhi |title=Onyeka Okongwu dominates as USC stays unbeaten in victory over Pepperdine |url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/usc/story/2019-11-19/onyeka-okongwu-dominates-usc-stays-unbeaten-victory-pepperdine |website=[[Los Angeles Times]] Basketball weekly awards |url=https://pac-12.com/article/2019/11/25/uscs-okongwu-first-sweep-pac-12-mens-basketball-weekly-awards |publisher=[[Pac-12 Conference]] |accessdate=January 27, 2020 |date=November 25, 2019}} On December 1, Okongwu recorded 27 points on 12-of-14 shooting, 14 rebounds and three blocks in a 77–62 victory over [[Harvard Crimson men's basketball|Harvard]] at the [[Orlando Invitational]].{{cite web |title=Onyeka Okongwu's 27 Points Lead USC Men's Basketball's 77-62 Rout Over Harvard |url=https://usctrojans.com/news/2019/12/1/usc-trojans-m-basketball-recap-harvard-crimson-espn-orlando-invitational-onyeka-okongwu.aspx |website=USC Athletics |publisher=[[Associated Press]] |accessdate=January 27, 2020 |date=December 1, 2019}} He scored 28 points, 24 of which came in the second half, and grabbed 12 rebounds in a December 15 win over [[Long Beach State men's basketball|Long Beach State]].{{cite web |title=Okongwu scores 28 in leading USC over Long Beach State 87-76 |url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/ncaab/2019/12/15/okongwu-scores-28-in-leading-usc-past-long-beach-state-87-76/40832271/ |website=[[USA Today]] |publisher=[[Associated Press]] 27, 2020 |date=December 16, 2019}} Okongwu continued his consistency into the Pac-12 season.
